name: Bhanga / Cannabis Sativa

sections.description_of_the_bhanga: Bhanga is the ancient medicinal herb, traditionally known by names such as Marijuana Indian hemp, Ganja. The scientific name of the plant is Cannabis Sativa. It belongs to the Cannabaceae family. Bhanga is known to be an annual herb with an erect stem, grows up to 3 to 10 feet or more than this and slightly branched with greyish green hair. The leaves of the plant are palmate, stipulate, present alternatively, have long petiole, smooth dark green with serrate, singly present, lanceolate, 3 to 11 in number, and acuminate leaflets. These are long up to 10 cm and wide up to 1.5 cm. leaflets have acute stipules at the base with tapering ends. These have basal leaves also present oppositely. These basal leaves are known as vegetative leaves. The flowers of the bhanga are small and unisexual kind. The female flower has five veined leaf encircled ovaries in a sheath. These are single, glandular and hairy. The ovary of the flower is one celled, and has a hanging ovule with thread-like stigmas. Their ovaries are very smooth and its stigma spreads out of the flower, about more than its length. The male one has five segments, almost present separately, downy with pale yellow color. The fruit of the bhanga is small and completely full of seeds. It is of brownish-grey color.
sections.general_description:
The Bhanga plant has been associated with ancient rituals and has been cultivated for its fibers, food, and medicinal properties. The drug has been explained from Vedic times, so famous with the name of vijaya in the medicinal field. Bhang was used as an intoxicant in India around 1000 BC.Bhanga is an integral part of Hindu culture. In the Atharvaveda, it is described as a beneficial herb known for its ability to relieve anxiety. It is also closely associated with Lord Shiva, who is often revered as its divine patron. It is used as Prasad on the celebration of Maha Shivratri festival. 
 The person who believes in Lord Shiva uses Bhang as the Prasad on the celebration of festival Maha Shivaratri. Solution of the Bhang Leaf herbs, Milk, Almond, Guava Leaf and other herbs are prepared on this day by the devotees of Lord Shiva. Bhang Pakora is one of the most famous and most usually used everywhere on Maha Shivratri. 
 Cannabis Sativa, scientific name of the bhang is a Latin name, in which sativa meant sown or cultivation. This plant has anti-inflammatory, sedative, anodyne, narcotic, neuralgic, anti-rheumatism, digestive, astringent, antispasmodic, aphrodisiac and diuretic properties. It is helpful in treating nervous disorders, gout, infantile convulsions, insomnia, gonorrhea, urinary infections, chronic cystitis and more. It is also known to give relief from strong pains, swelling, wounds and dandruff. 
 Bhanga is enriched with plenty of phytochemicals. This plant contains over 60 cannabinoids and approximately 140 terpenes. Its primary chemical constituents include cannabine, cannabinol, cannabidiolic acid, cannabielsoin, cannabichromene, tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), cannabicyclol, and cannabigerol, among other diverse cannabinoids. These are found in the roots of the plant. Essential oils of plant parts contain terpenes. Fruits and roots comprise lignanamides and phenolic amides. 
 CLASSIFICATION 

 Kingdom – Plantae 
 Subkingdom – Tracheobionta 
 Superdivision – Spermatophyta 
 Division – Magnoliophyta 
 Class – Magnoliopsida 
 Subclass – Hamamelididae 
 Order – Urticales
sections.habitat:
It is the native to central Asia. It is grown in Asia, Europe, Iran, Iraq, Pakistan and China. Bhanga has been cultivated from ancient times in India since 900BC. Then in the medieval period, it was brought to North Africa. In India, cultivation of this plant is controlled and grown in some areas only.it is wild in north western Indian regions such as Rajasthan, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Bihar. These areas are Nainital, Garhwal, Uttar Pradesh, Almora and Amritsar. It is also cultivated in the areas of Kashmir, Nepal and Taravancore but up to little extent. 
 NAMES OF THE BHANGA 

 Sanskrit Name – Vijaya, Ananda, Bahuvadini, Banga, Bhanga, Bhangi, Bhringi, Bhringi, Bijeeah, Chapala

 Bhanga is known to have nerve stimulant properties, so helps to give relief in nervous exhaustion, periodical headaches, migraine, nervous vomiting, delirium, neuralgia and convulsions. 
 Bhanga is traditionally used as an appetizer and is known to provide relief from digestive issues such as bowel disorders and dyspepsia. 
 The leaves of the plant are used to treat the problem of insomnia. 
 Their leaves are also used to give relief in resolving tumors, itching problems, skin diseases, wounds and sores. 
 It is very useful in giving relief from head lice and dandruff. 
 Bhanga is very useful in case of diarrhea, plies and dysentery. 
 This is used in the cases of inflammations and hemorrhoids. 
 It is known to have aphrodisiac properties. 
 It is very useful in eye disorders like in photophobia. 
 It is used as a remedy for malaria, black water fever and blood poisoning.

 Seeds 
 Resins (Charas) 
 Flowers (Ganja) 
 
 DOSAGE 
 
 Bhangs leaf powder – 125 to 250 mg 
 Ganja – 50 to 125 mg 
 Charas – 30 mg 
 
 PRECAUTIONS TO BE TAKEN 
 
 It is unsafe during pregnancy and lactation. 
 It should not be taken in the case of high blood pressure. 
 It should not be taken for a long time and in high doses as it causes depression, anxiety, decreases immunity and testosterone, sperm quality and number.
